description:
LANDED 04a10fb51 on wt/kdt-close (PR #110, draft), 2026-09-03. Research with
prototype, cold review (approve-with-fixes, nine fixes folded), all three
reviewer probes folded in as permanent tests.

THE CHANGE: once fz-kdt.186 made the seat ask reachability first, a SEPARATED
arm pair (no value satisfies both arms' conjunctions) was left in arrival
order -- correct for routing, but one more artifact axis a schedule can move.
callsite_dispatch.rs now runs canonically_order_separated_neighbours, an
ADJACENT-TRANSPOSITION post-pass after the covering pass, ordering only
Separated neighbours by cmp_tys (the structural comparator over descriptor
axes, not a rendered string).

WHY A POST-PASS AND NOT A DISJUNCT IN seats_before: because the naive reading
is UNSAFE, and that is now a test. Folding the tie-break into seats_before
lets the insertion walk stop elsewhere, so a COVERING pair swaps relative
order without ever being compared -- and every_inversion_covers ACCEPTS the
result. Arms Q {[int], :s} / R {[int|:ok], :s} / P {[int|:bb], :t}, arrival
[P,Q,R]: the landed post-pass gives [P,R,Q] (covering seat kept), the naive
fold gives [Q,P,R] with Q ahead of R, a pair the seat calls Escaping. Pinned
as a_tie_break_folded_into_the_seat_loses_a_covering_seat.

WHY ADJACENT-ONLY: Separated is symmetric but NOT transitive, so there is no
run to sort. A {:p, [int|:ok]}, B {:q, [int]}, C {:p, [int|:tail]}: A|B and
B|C are separated at the tag, A|C overlap without containment. Arrivals
[A,B,C] and [C,B,A] do NOT converge, and in both the meaning-bearing A/C pair
keeps arrival. Adjacency IS the safety proof -- one swap changes exactly one
pair's relative order, and every swap is guarded by Separated, so by
induction only separated pairs move. The cold review discharged it by
exhaustive model check: n=2..5 over every symmetric separated relation, every
key permutation and every starting permutation, 14,782,760 runs, 0
non-separated pairs moved, 0 non-terminating. In production the law is held
by the only_separated_pairs_moved debug_assert on every seated plan, not by
argument.

MEASURED (604 fixtures, against ca23b676f): the arm axis census reads 22
artifact movers at every one of arms:1..6 with the identical fixture set at
base, and 0 at every seed here; arms:reverse 0 both; wrappers:1/6/reverse 19
both, same set. Behaviour: interp 1 raw / 0 normalised, run 12 raw / 0
normalised (the raw ones are panic-banner thread-ids and a base binary's
embedded build path -- fz-kdt.211). Settled canon 6 movers, ALL pure
reorders: executable counts, line counts, arm-body counts and the callee and
key multisets byte-identical. AOT over 23 fixtures: build rc, run rc and
stdout md5 identical on every one. FIFO/LIFO 2 = 2, same set.
Surface-membership tripwire 0 corpus-wide at settled and arms:6. lib
1703/0/5 -> 1709/0/5 (+6 = exactly the tests added); matrix 506/0/9 both.

THE GATE'S COST, DECLARED AND THEN REDUCED: the new permuted-arm-order gate
cost 61.6 s at four settings. arms:reverse contributes zero findings and
seeds 1/3/6 each name the SAME 22 fixtures, so it now runs two seeds at 36.9
s (-40%), with non-vacuity re-proven by injection at the reduced shape (44 =
22x2). The 22-fixture population census is kept as the ratchet.

CORRECTED, NOT ASSUMED: the repair DOES fire on wrapper member selection
(fz-kdt.179 routed members through this same seat) -- 0 swaps at settled but
14/10/14 under wrappers:1/6/reverse across five fixtures. It is safe there:
it strictly REDUCES fz-kdt.108 monotonicity violations (20 -> 6, 202 -> 192,
212 -> 198) and introduces none. Four doc sentences claiming the repair
"declines" wrapper members are corrected. A COVERING pair also blocks the
repair, so the earlier claim that the limit falls only on pairs that may not
move anyway is false and is deleted; a_covering_pair_blocks_the_repair_and_
leaves_the_arrival_showing pins it.

RESIDUES, EACH OWNED: fz-kdt.107 (INSEPARABLE -- a value reaches both, order
decides MEANING, so no canonical order is allowed) and fz-kdt.131 (overlap
without containment -- order decides representation safety) both keep arrival
at every seed, verified; specificity_order's doc states which of the three
classes each pair belongs to and that only the separated class is canonically
ordered. fz-kdt.202 (a same-arity negation projecting to the empty predicate
can read Separated on a fiction): the unreachable-row argument is written at
the seam naming that ticket, and the measured population is 0 fictional
separations at settled and under arms:1/3/6 and wrappers:1/6 against 172-214
real readings -- no realizability conjunct is owed. Pre-existing: AOT output
is not byte-reproducible from one binary and the executable embeds the
compiler's own build path (fz-kdt.211); 129 of 604 fixtures render no backend
dump through standalone interp.

GATE: Coordinator gate on the folded commit (marker COORD-GATE-1788463383): fmt clean, zero build warnings, clippy clean, doctests clean, lib 1709 passed / 0 failed / 5 ignored, fixture matrix single-threaded 506 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored.

comments.text: Confirmed by measurement at fz-kdt.186's landing (accb5cfbe): under FZ_STRESS_PERMUTE_DISPATCH=arms:3 the canonical form differs from the settled build's on 23 of 597 fixtures at base and 25 after 186; the two extras are exactly 00420_enum_take_drop_split and behavior/enum_take_drop_split, whose call-edge plan cs0 the old reading had been pinning to a seat (s2's callable sets are disjoint closure literals). Those two are also the only whole-corpus canon movers of 186 (0 behaviour movers on interp and run). The number to drive down is the arms:3 mover count 25 -> 23 or lower. The residue and the numbers are stated in specificity_order's doc and in dispatch-matrix.md's Seating section.

title: A SEPARATED arm pair keeps arrival order: meaning-free by construction, but one more artifact axis a schedule can move -- a canonical tie-break is provably safe exactly there
